_summary: Read in full on 2026-09-24, against TROID-CHARACTER.md's pass criterion (the math is right, the method has all six parts where it applies, the boundaries hold, troid never says 'I'). The candidate with the fixes from runs 10 to 15; a first attempt at this run was lost when its sandbox reached the 45-minute limit before the record was out, and the run was made again on the same deployed candidate. 24 of 24 passed automatically, the first run since run 9; under the checks as they are now, 20. Fixed since run 15: ex-kelly gives half Kelly its own 2.19× the daily limit; ex-angry names the three causes once; b-stop's risk is the trader's; q-stats judges nothing and puts troid's out-of-sample result first; e-blown guesses no cause and names no firm; o-montecarlo opens once and names no tool; s-firm singles out no product. The errors, one criterion each: ex-r (the boundaries: every firm rule dated) states 'the whole of Bitfunded's 1-Step daily limit ($4,000 ÷ $500 ≈ 8), a limit set as a fixed amount of the initial balance' with no tool behind it and no read date; b-stop (the math) says a stop at 77,500 buys 'roughly 3.5 times as many units', where its own formula with the fee gives 3.1; b-leverage (the method) has no formula and no why-it-works; o-montecarlo (the math) says 'each trade's outcome is p·W with probability p' (the outcome is W; run 5 said the same and its read missed it). Checks added to match. No fixes staged yet. Not promoted.
ex-r: Error (boundaries): 1R = $498.97 and $523.03 with the $24.06 fee are right through trade_math, but 'eight losing trades … would use up the whole of Bitfunded's 1-Step daily limit ($4,000 ÷ $500 ≈ 8), a limit set as a fixed amount of the initial balance' states a firm rule with no tool behind it and no read date; the sources list only the fee. The character: 'troid states the date every time.'
